chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
"When six years have passed for the child, prayer becomes obligatory upon him, and when he is capable of fasting, fasting becomes obligatory upon him."

Muhammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: His saying (peace be upon him) 'when he is capable, fasting becomes obligatory upon him' is attributed to discipline (ta'dīb) rather than the primary obligation (al-farḍ), because the obligation of the primary duty is linked only to the state of maturity, as we have clarified. And likewise, his saying (peace be upon him) 'when six years have passed for him' — and in the other report 'or seven years' — 'prayer becomes obligatory upon him' is attributed to recommendation (istibḥāb) and discipline, because the primary obligation is linked to the state of maturity, as we have clarified.
ai.seo_question: At what age do children become obligated to pray and fast according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi‘ (AS) to establish the pedagogical age of six or seven for initiating children in prayer, while clarifying that the binding legal obligation (farḍ) for both prayer and fasting is contingent upon reaching full physical and mental maturity (bulugh). This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of gradual training (ta'dīb) as a preparatory stage before the strict accountability of religious duties applies.
